title: A Study of Situational Reasoning for Traffic Understanding

problem.claim: Traffic situation understanding requires fusion of perceptual information with domain-specific and causal commonsense knowledge.

gap.claim: It remains unclear whether models can align these information sources and reason in novel traffic scenarios.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces three text-based traffic situational-reasoning tasks: BDD-QA for situational decision-making, TV-QA for complex event causality, and HDT-QA for human driving exams.

The paper applies four knowledge-enhanced methods based on natural language inference, commonsense knowledge-graph self-supervision, multi-QA joint training, and dense retrieval of domain information, pairing them with relevant knowledge sources.
The paper benchmarks knowledge-aware methods across the three datasets under zero-shot evaluation and analyzes performance by data partitions and prediction categories.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the three text-based situational-reasoning tasks as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive zero-shot experiments benchmarking various knowledge-aware methods against the three datasets.
The authors report in-depth analyses of model performance on data partitions and categorical examinations of model predictions.

narrative_sequence.summary: Traffic monitoring could improve road safety, security, and smart-city infrastructure.
Traffic understanding requires combining perceptual information with domain-specific and causal commonsense knowledge.
Prior benchmarks and methods do not resolve whether models align these information sources and reason in novel scenarios.
The authors introduce three traffic reasoning tasks and apply four knowledge-enhanced methods linked to relevant knowledge sources.
The authors conduct zero-shot benchmarking and analyze performance across partitions and prediction categories.
